title: Trump's trade war - 6 months later
summary: Money & Macro review of the first six months of the 2025 trade war: little inflation so far, slower growth, a weaker dollar, and reindustrialization not yet visible.

assertions.quote: tariffs have not caused much inflation in the United States

verdicts.note: Through mid-2025 headline CPI stayed near 2.7% and core goods rose modestly; front-loaded inventories and partial absorption by firms delayed the pass-through.

The consumer price effect does not arrive at once: about half the direct effect is in place after three months and all of it by six, while the indirect effect more than doubles between six and twelve months, so by mid-2025 only part of the eventual effect (2.9 points on goods inflation by February 2026) had reached consumers.

assertions.quote: foreign exporters are paying 53% of us there so far
tariff uncertainty is making it difficult for firms to make investment decisions all around the world
So tariffs are bad for economic growth, and that prediction is holding up quite well so far.

verdicts.note: Forecasters cut 2025 growth after the tariffs and business investment weakened, but actual output held up better than expected, so the drag was real but modest.

assertions.quote: the prediction that the Trump tariffs would increase the value of the dollar is not holding up at all

verdicts.note: The dollar index fell roughly 10% in the first half of 2025 as foreign investors rotated out of US assets, the opposite of the textbook tariff effect.
The dollar depreciated over the 2025 tariff period, which raised import prices further, but the post does not attribute the depreciation to tariffs or to investors pulling back from U.S. assets.

assertions.quote: there are bringing in a lot of money, but not enough to make up for Trump's massive tax cuts

verdicts.note: CBO scored the 2025 tax law at over $3 trillion of added deficits against tariff revenue of a few hundred billion a year.

assertions.quote: this included projects that they were going to be doing anyway

verdicts.note: Measured business fixed investment and foreign direct investment in 2025 ran near historical baselines, far below the pledged totals.
